headline: Curriculum Committee discussed educational technology policy, assessment calendar, and meeting schedule; tabled summer updates to next meeting.
summary: The committee reviewed upcoming meeting dates and locations through March 2026, and discussed a reporting schedule for K-3 assessment data tied to the district's 'Leaning into learning' focus. Members held an extended discussion on educational technology, including state legislation, cell phone policy compliance, AI use, device liability, and communication with families. The Summer Updates item was tabled to the next meeting.
decisions: Tabled the Summer Updates item to the next meeting.

decision_evidence.quote:
Summer Updates (k/1 changes to foundational skills, universal screener set to begin in September Grades 1-11, math professional learning set for K-12, Aug 4 ILT retreat)
Tabled to next meeting

plain_text:
Curriculum Committee Meeting - Aug 25 2026 Minutes 
Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 4:00 PM 
Central Office, 150 Colchester Avenue, Conference Room 21 
Present: Matthew Price, Gary Golden, Tom Flanagan, Lauren Klaffey, Katherine Grykien,  Polly 
Vanderputton, Melissa Zygmant 
 
 
1. Opening  
A. Call meeting to order   
4:05pm  
B. Suspend Robert's Rules 
 
2. Public Comment 
None 
 
3. Discussion  
A. Update on committee meeting time from the board 
 Sept 22 - At Central Office 
 Oct 27 - At Central Office 
 Nov 17 - At Central Office 
 Dec 8 - At Board Meeting Location 
 Jan 26 - At Central Office 
 Feb 16 - At Board Meeting Location 
 March 23 - At Central Office 
 Future Dates TBD at a later time  
B. Assessment calendar - so the committee can prepare to discuss at which meetings. 
 Leaning into learning this year. The focus is on K-3. Focus will be on growth in that 
cohort. 
 The committee discussed a reporting cycle based on the screening data to be 
shared with the curriculum committee and eventually the full board. 
o VTCAP Reporting Cycle - share that at Sept Meeting 
o Reporting on First Assessment Data in October 
o Reporting on Second Assessment Data in Feb 
o Reporting on Third Assessment Data TBD (Likely June) 
 Data will be shared disaggregated by Free and Reduced Lunch and Non-Free and 
Reduced Lunch as well as overall 
 There was a mention of the importance to consider how to help the 4-12 graders 
who may need more assistance at this time.  
����������� 
Draft
C. Educational Technology: Review of State Legislation, Community Feedback, and 
District Planning 
 Discussion of tech in the classroom. 
 Strong national discussion about the use of tech in classrooms. 
 Melissa Zymgant shared a copy of the distraction-free schools policy. 
 There was a discussion about the liability of the districts for providing these tech 
tools to students, given the nature of the EULA that parents must agree to. 
 It was highlighted that there is a broad evaluation of how the community and 
constituents want changes to technology use in the classroom. 
 Discussion of the rapid evolution of technology in schools and the classroom. 
 Need to educate families on how to communicate with schools now that dedicated 
devices for students are not available. 
 The district is having lots of conversations about tech in schools, but conversations 
have been somewhat siloed. 
o Concerns about compliance with the cell phone policy in BHS 
o Conversations about AI and policies associated with the use of AI in school 
o Revising tech use agreement, which is where many schools have taken the 
moment to dictate restrictions 
o Key components are missing - parent engagement/education with the 
community about how to tackle this challenge 
 Concern about the barrier between school-owned devices and child’s use of these 
devices outside of school (which happens in upper grades). 
o Access to devices may be a liability given what can be accessed. 
 Concern about different groups with different cultural beliefs or perceptions about 
education that may differentially impact students from different backgrounds. 
o How do New American families view devices as the primary modality for 
education? 
 Concerns that the district is playing “whack-a-mole” in trying to police different 
software choices of the day. 
 Discussion about the pedagogical approach for using these devices 
o Students are required to turn in most writing assignments via Chromebook, 
but students are not taught typing practice. Does this create a burden for 
students when generating text? 
 Discussion about internet safety and appropriate use of the internet among 
devices that are sent home, especially in High School when the devices are 
“unlocked” 
 Thinking about how AI will impact the curriculum - how do we help students 
become more useful than AI for the future. 
o How does this influence strategic planning goals 
 Next Steps: 
o Strategies to communicate effectively with parents about these changes 
o Further review of the liability associated with these tools 
o Discussion of the curriculum shifts required to move away from the 
integration of tech into the classrooms 
o Suggestion to shift internal discussion

 Include in the survey about belongingness to have more tech-focused questions to 
gauge the broader community about these policies.  
D. Summer Updates (k/1 changes to foundational skills, universal screener set to begin 
in September Grades 1-11, math professional learning set for K-12, Aug 4 ILT retreat) 
Tabled to next meeting 
 
4. Adjournment
